decisions.reason: The mitred lever family shares production and finishing with the core range, so holding it costs little, and two years without a clear negative signal still leave its value uncertain enough to keep the option open.
The multifunctional handle fits the firm's barrier-free and accessibility direction, and as a single model it is cheap to keep while its market response becomes clearer.
The withdrawal of the similar lever line A shows that weak lever families get pruned, but D has shown no negative result yet and its low holding cost justifies waiting one more year.
The German Design Award and its own dedicated page indicate the collection's value is being realized, which supports further commitment rather than abandonment.
The finish uses existing finishing capability across many product families at minimal cost, so it remains a cheap option to hold while demand develops.
